title: JSON import
description:
import_json() happy path with round trip, plus validation and atomicity.

[T11] Implement import_json(data) for valid input with defaults for optional fields, preserving ids, updating the id counter, returning count. Tests in tests/test_import.py.
[T12] Add full validation to import_json: validate everything before mutating the store. Tests in tests/test_import_validation.py.
acceptance_criteria: ids preserved and later add() gets id greater than max existing
export -> import into a new TodoList yields equal items
invalid JSON, non-list top level, non-object items raise ValidationError
empty text, bad priority, non-bool complete, bad due_date, non-int/bool id, missing id or text raise ValidationError
duplicate ids within the data or against existing items raise ValidationError
after any failure the list is unchanged (atomic)
spec_description: A tiny in-memory to-do library in Python (package `todo`, class `TodoList` in todo/__init__.py or todo.py) with custom exceptions `TodoError` (base, subclass of Exception), `ItemNotFoundError` (subclass of TodoError and KeyError-free; message includes the unknown id) and `ValidationError` (subclass of TodoError and ValueError). Items are represented by a dataclass `TodoItem` with fields: id (int, auto-incremented from 1, never reused), text (str), complete (bool, default False), due_date (datetime.date or None), priority ('high'|'medium'|'low', default 'medium'). All features are methods on `TodoList`, each covered by pytest tests in tests/.
